The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from the Met Office and other agencies indicate a maximum temperature of 24–25°C for London on September 7, 2026, driven by mild westerly airflow, partial afternoon clearing after morning cloud, and typical early-September insolation under variable high pressure. Historical September averages near 20°C provide context, but current steering patterns and dew points favor the upper end of the daily range without reaching 26°C thresholds. Updated observations through midday and any late-model adjustments will refine resolution criteria for the day's peak reading.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current forecasts for Beijing on September 7, 2026, converge on a daily maximum of 28–30 °C, directly supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward 29 °C (54 %) and 30 °C (40 %).** Multiple numerical weather models and official guidance (including Chinese Meteorological Administration equivalents and international sources such as GFS-derived products) indicate peak readings near 29–30 °C during the afternoon hours, with values climbing from morning readings around 24–27 °C before cooling under increasing cloud cover and showers.

Key scientific drivers include moderate solar insolation under partly cloudy to overcast skies, which limits surface heating compared with clear-sky September norms; northeasterly flow advecting slightly cooler maritime air; and scattered precipitation (60–85 % chance in many runs) that enhances evaporative cooling and reduces the diurnal temperature range. Historical climatology places the early-September average high near 27.9 °C, so today’s pattern sits modestly above the baseline yet remains well below late-summer extremes.

Model consensus shows little support for 31 °C or higher, consistent with the market’s low single-digit probabilities for those outcomes. Traders appear to be pricing the tight clustering of reliable forecast guidance around the 29–30 °C threshold, with resolution depending on the precise official maximum recorded by Beijing’s primary observing stations. Updated model runs or real-time observations through the afternoon could still shift the final reading within the narrow 28–31 °C window.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the King Abdulaziz International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=oejn

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast consensus from multiple meteorological models positions 37°C as the most probable daily maximum for Jeddah on September 7, 2026, aligning with the market’s leading 47.5% implied probability.** Coastal Red Sea influence and typical late-summer atmospheric conditions—high pressure, light northwest winds, and low precipitation risk—support peak heating in the mid-to-upper 30s Celsius during afternoon hours. Historical September averages near 35–37°C provide climatological context, while current observations and short-range guidance show stable, humid conditions with dew points in the low-to-mid 20s that limit extreme outliers. Slight model spread accounts for the secondary probabilities on 36°C and 38°C, with resolution hinging on the precise hourly peak recorded at official stations.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Miami Intl Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 7 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=kmia

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

This aligns with September climatology for the region, where average highs hover around 89–90°F, modulated by sea-breeze convergence and high dew points near 78–80°F that elevate heat indices above 100°F without altering the dry-bulb maximum. Recent model runs show limited spread, with the strongest consensus on 90–91°F and modest upside risk to 92–93°F if convective initiation is delayed. Market-implied odds reflect this narrow uncertainty range, with traders weighting the latest NWS guidance and short-term observational trends from Miami International Airport.

Recent model runs show afternoon peaks around 22 °C before showers intensify, consistent with the market’s tight clustering between 22 °C and 23 °C. Resolution hinges on the precise reading at the official observatory station; any break in cloud cover or delayed rainfall could nudge the peak toward 24 °C or higher, while stronger or earlier convection would favor 21 °C or below.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Clear skies, light northerly winds, and stable high-pressure conditions are positioning Seoul/Incheon for a daytime maximum near 28°C on September 8, 2026, consistent with the market’s heaviest weighting on that outcome (46%).** 

Official and model guidance from sources including the Korea Meteorological Administration, WeatherBug, Met Office, and Yr.no converge on highs of 28–29°C (82–84°F) under mostly sunny to partly cloudy skies, with minimal precipitation risk and dew points supporting efficient daytime heating. Recent days have seen similar peaks (27–29°C) amid a post-summer cooling pattern, and the absence of significant cloud cover or stronger onshore flow tomorrow supports the narrow 27–29°C cluster that dominates trader pricing. 

Lower probabilities on 30°C+ or sub-27°C reflect limited upside from anomalous warmth and low downside risk from unexpected cooling or increased cloudiness. Short-term model runs remain stable this close to the event, with any final adjustments likely tied to the next official KMA update or real-time observations from Incheon International Airport.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 8 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zgsz

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mpmg

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus and current atmospheric conditions in Panama City, Panama, show typical September rainy-season setup with high humidity and scattered afternoon convection, creating tight uncertainty around peak daytime heating. Historical averages near 29–30°C provide baseline context, yet reduced cloud cover or delayed thunderstorm development could push maxima to 34°C or higher on September 8. Traders assign roughly even weight to 33°C, 34°C, and 35°C-plus outcomes because forecast guidance diverges on exact timing and intensity of showers, which directly cap or allow brief radiative heating. Updated runs from regional models and local observations in the next 24 hours will likely refine these probabilities before resolution.
